category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.title='When the child confuses LEFT and RIGHT' and the lesson body do not bridge to or from neighbouring days; there is no explicit cross-reference to Lesson 2's positional words or to the recording arc in Lesson 3.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a one-sentence forward-bridge in consolidation/teacher_script that names what's coming next (e.g., 'Tomorrow Bot HIDES — we'll use ABOVE, BELOW, BESIDE, BETWEEN to find him; today's direction words still tell us how to MOVE there'). Have Bot reference the unit arc explicitly so children carry the thread.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough trap = 'left/right hand-side mix-up' with recovery_moves=['Use L stickers.', 'Drill L for left.', 'Compare with body.']. The trap is real for K but is not cited to research and the recovery does NOT branch by what the diagnostic told you about the child.
category_feedback.required_fix: Reframe trap as egocentric frame-of-reference (Clements & Sarama 2009): child treats left/right as fixed in the room, not relative to body — when Bot turns, child's 'left' no longer matches Bot's. BRANCH recovery: (a) knows own left but mis-applies — rotate child to face Bot first; (b) can't identify own left — L-sticker hand-check; (c) correct with sticker not without — fade stickers.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: lesson_specific_materials lists 'Coding Floor Mat (1 per pair)' and 'Arrow Cards (20)' as required, and differentiation.for_movement_learners='Walk a tape grid on classroom floor' is offered only as a learner-style option, not as a no-paper, no-purchase fallback for the whole class.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add an explicit no-paper, no-purchase pathway in the lesson body (not just differentiation). In action steps write: 'NO-MATERIALS VERSION: skip mat and arrow cards — masking-tape a 4x4 grid on the carpet (or 16 sticky notes); children BECOME Bot, stepping square to square as caller says forward/back/left/right. Teacher's pointing arm replaces arrow cards; whole lesson runs on voice and body.'

category_feedback.specific_evidence: consolidation.exit_routine='Each child names ONE direction: "Forward!"' — there is no distinctive carry-between-lessons chant or sentence frame; Bot's 'BEEP BOOP' is in the hook only and the closing has no memorable refrain children would still chant on Day 5.
category_feedback.required_fix: Give Bot a distinctive quotable refrain that closes EVERY lesson and is introduced here in Lesson 1. Concrete: Bot's call-and-response 'BEEP BOOP — who moves the bot? YOU DO!' with children chanting back 'YOU DO!' Add this verbatim to consolidation.exit_routine and teacher_script so Lessons 2-5 can reuse it. The chant must appear in the lesson text, not only inferred.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough names the trap as a hand-side mix-up rather than a research-grounded spatial-reasoning misconception, and the action steps do not let children invent or compare alternative routes — every step is teacher-called ('Move 4', 'Stretch: include turns'). No moment where two pairs compare different sequences that arrive at the same square.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add an invent-and-compare beat in action: after step 3, two pairs share 4-step routes to the SAME target and notice 'we got there a different way!' Cite the principle in expanded_walkthrough.rationale by name — egocentric-vs-allocentric spatial reasoning (Clements & Sarama 2009; Battista 2007). One rationale sentence plus the compare-routes move lifts this to exceeding.

summary: Lesson 1 is solidly built — Bot is consistent, success criteria are 'I can' style, materials are mostly everyday, and the worksheet maps cleanly to the lesson's success criteria with a transfer task in Part 3. But four categories sit at 3: the trap is real-but-thin and recovery doesn't branch, there is no all-class no-paper fallback, no carry-between-lessons chant, and the math reasoning lacks an invent-or-compare moment with research-grounded framing. Worksheet is fine — fixes belong in lesson_01.
